newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Unions say 83 pct of Argentines heed strike call.
newsitem.headline: Unions say 83 pct of Argentines heed strike call.

text.p: Argentina's main labor federation said 83 percent of Argentines heeded the union call and went out on general strike Thursday.

"The turnout was at least 83 percent and we thank and salute the working people and the immense majority of the Argentine people," CGT federation chief Rodolfo Daer told a late afternoon news conference.
But the Labor Ministry said earlier Thursday that only about 31 percent of Argentine workers joined the stoppage in protest against decrees to make labor markets more flexible.

Daer said the CGT "rejects lower salaries, rejects a more precarious life for workers; it rejects freeing the eight-hour working day limit; the 48-hour-a-week limit; that workers should be exposed to their employers in an arbitrary way. We have rejected this, we continued rejecting this and we are going to continue rejecting it."
The CGT called its third strike this year after President Carlos Menem lost patience in talks with the unions to hammer out a compromise over the laws, which are aimed at reducing employers' costs.

The president passed the laws by decree, provoking unions into following up a 24-hour stoppage in August against Menem's free-market policies and their successful September strike. The government, which said it plans more labor decrees, hopes a more flexible employment market will help reduce the country's 17.3 percent jobless rate.
